title: What If a Rip Current Caught You? Don't Swim Straight

scenes.text: What if a rip current grabbed you at the beach? The danger isn't being pulled under.
Rip currents can move faster than an Olympic swimmer, over eight feet per second at their strongest.
They never pull you underwater. They carry you away from the shore, out past the breaking waves.
Fighting straight back is the trap. You tire fast, and panic does the rest.
Swim parallel to the shore until you leave the current, then angle back in.
Rip currents cause over eighty percent of surf beach rescues. Knowing this is the whole escape.

description:
What if a rip current caught you at the beach?
It moves faster than an Olympic swimmer, but it only carries you out, never under.
